plan.notes: Source: Otterbein University Department of Biology and Earth Science official 'Suggested Program of Study' for the Zoo Track in the Zoo & Conservation Science Major (BA). SUGGESTED SEQUENCE — explicitly a suggested program of study. No explicit catalog year on the document; the PDF footer carries revision stamp 2/18/26, so catalog year is recorded as 2025-2026. Credit ranges resolved at minimums with disclosure: 'BIO 3000 elective 3-4' slots at 3; 'ZOSC 4900 Internship (optional) or Elective 4-6' at 4; SYE 2-3 at 2. Term totals as transcribed (minimums): 14+15+16+16+14.5+15.5+15+14 = 120, matching the 120 hours required to graduate (footnote f). TRANSCRIPTION JUDGMENT (disclosed): in the spring of sophomore year the extracted text shows two overlapping ZOSC practica rows ('ZOSC 2011' and 'ZOSC 2010/2012 Wildlife Practica'); transcribing both would total 18 against the source's printed term total of 16, so the term is transcribed as a single 2-credit choice slot (ZOSC 2010, 2011, or 2012) consistent with source footnote b (at least one course from ZOSC 2010/2011/2012 required) and the printed total of 16. BIO 3020 may be taken any semester of junior or senior year per the source; it is shown in fall junior year where the source grids it. The 'BIO 3000 elective or ZOSC 4950 Research (optional)' fall-senior row is one or-slot transcribed at 3. Fourteen credits must come from BIO 3000-3999 (not counting 3020 twice), EQSC 4000, or ZOSC 4950/BIO 4998 WI per footnote c. Courses marked '(skills)'/'(recommended)' carry the source's annotations. No TCCNS in Ohio; transfer_confidence left empty. BIO 3998 is taken in both semesters of junior year by program design (two semesters required per source footnote d); allow_repeated_courses is set.
